content.title: Building Code updates coming in 2026
content.summary: The City of Arvada will update its building codes in 2026, introducing significant changes that will affect builders, designers, homeowners, and business owners. Key updates include the adoption of wildfire codes for structures in high-risk areas, new energy codes that promote electric and solar readiness, and the requirement for sprinkler systems in new single-family homes and townhomes. These changes aim to enhance safety, energy efficiency, and compliance with modern construction practices.
content.body:
The City of Arvada is updating its building codes in 2026. This is a necessary and normal change that the City makes periodically, but it will come with some changes that will impact builders, designers, developers, homeowners, and business owners. Read on for more information on what's changing and why, along with what you can do to be prepared.

## What are building codes?

Building codes are minimum requirements for construction that keep our community safe in the places that we live, sleep, eat, and play. They protect affordability, structural strength, means of egress, stability, sanitation, light and ventilation, energy conservation and safety to life and property from fire and other hazards.

## Why are they changing?

Building codes are updated by municipalities every three to six years to keep up with industry practices, innovations in the construction industry, new products, new materials and new methods of construction. Updates also ensure consistency across city lines, which helps contractors. The updates in the 2024 International Codes reflect the latest national standards for building safety, energy performance and modern construction practices.

## What are the big changes, and what will they impact?

As we enter into this code adoption cycle, the biggest changes that builders, designers, developers, homeowners, and business owners will notice will revolve around wildfire codes, energy codes, and residential home sprinkler systems.

### Wildfire codes

The City has adopted the Arvada Wildfire Resiliency Code, our first wildfire codes, which will have requirements for structural hardening and defensible space for certain structures that are within the wildland urban interface areas. This will primarily affect new construction but will also mean some changes to the exterior of existing structures and the maintenance requirements of existing structures that are within identified risk areas. [Read more about the wildfire code in the FAQ](https://www.arvadaco.gov/m/faq?cat=105) or[**search by address**](https://arvada.maps.arcgis.com/apps/instant/lookup/index.html?appid=e436198a1e0045bbbab18b1cf359cb6d) to see if you are in one of the identified risk areas.

### Energy codes

Our energy codes will now incorporate electric-ready, solar-ready, and electric vehicle (EV)-ready requirements through the adoption of the Colorado Low Energy Carbon Code, which is based on the 2024 International Energy Conservation Code. These changes are geared toward preparing our built environments for new energy technologies by reducing the future costs of retrofitting. The new energy codes will increase flexibility for builders by providing new pathways of compliance; they can help homeowners save money on energy bills by improving efficiency and reducing energy consumption.

### Residential home sprinkler systems

Finally, there will be changes surrounding sprinkler systems. Sprinkler systems are already required for certain commercial buildings and residential buildings; these changes will require sprinkler systems to be installed in new single family homes, duplexes and townhomes.  It is important to note that these changes would not impact existing homes.

You can read a full description of the changes on the [Detailed changes page](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1446/14801/New-Building-Codes-2026).

## How do I know if I'm impacted?

In general:

- **If you are planning to perform any construction, renovation, alteration, remodel, repair, demolition, change of occupancy, etc.:** You may be subject to new requirements. In general, building permits submitted before July 1, 2026, can use the 2018 codes, and permits submitted after July 1 will need to comply with the newly updated codes. Please contact the Building Safety Division at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#2c4e5945404845424b5c495e4145585f6c4d5e5a4d484d02435e4b) if you have questions.
- **If you have an ongoing or issued building permit that was issued with approval under our current codes:** Your project should not be affected by these changes as long as your permit remains in good status, is not abandoned, work continues to progress, etc. Please continue to work through your permit processes and inspections to ensure compliance. For more about whether wildfire codes will affect you, [view the FAQ](https://www.arvadaco.gov/m/faq?cat=105).
- **For development projects currently in the development application stage, or which have master permits that are approved or under review:**We have created an implementation plan to assist these projects. Under this implementation plan, most development projects will be able to align with our currently adopted building codes (2018) and may not be affected by these new changes. We feel that having a thoughtful plan in place to assist contractors and our community in finding solutions through these changes is important. We encourage those going through these stages to reach out to the Building Safety Division with questions or to review your project and go over what to expect.

## When will these changes occur?

These codes were approved by Arvada City Council on March 24, 2026, and will be formally adopted on April 1, 2026. Implementation will begin on July 1, 2026.

## More information

- [For builders: Detailed changes coming in 2026](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1446/14801/New-Building-Codes-2026)
- [For home and business owners: Prepare your property for wildfire](https://www.arvadaco.gov/1447/14804/New-Building-Codes-2026)

## Questions?

As City staff implement these changes, updates will be made to the City of Arvada website explaining timelines and impacts. Watch this page for the latest information. If you have questions about any of the upcoming changes, please do not hesitate to reach out to the Building Division at [[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#4220372b2e262b2c253227302f2b3631022330342326236c2d3025).
